title: E0121: Assert with user-controlled string
plain_english: Calling `assert()` with a string argument that contains user-controlled input can lead to code execution. In older PHP versions, string arguments to `assert()` are evaluated as PHP code.
why_matters: `assert()` with a string argument can act as a code execution sink: - An attacker may be able to execute arbitrary PHP code - It can lead to full server compromise - String arguments to `assert()` were deprecated in PHP 7.2 and removed in PHP 8.0
what_it_checks: `assert()` calls where the argument is a string containing tainted input
String concatenation inside `assert()` with user-controlled variables
